why: Drag and wheel only filled inertial offsets with or without a scene, and the camera moved only on _beforeRender frames, as the source's applyInertia confirms.
Direct limit fields clamp no write, but interpolateArcRotateCamera reads them directly: with upperRadiusLimit 12 written by hand a radius goal of 100 settles at 12.
Clamping is immediate and later limit fields are honoured, but the offset is zeroed only when a bound is hit: radius = 15 inside the limits keeps inertialRadiusOffset 0.5.
pitch = 1 at radius 4R read 0.001 and stayed lost after a radius write, while setGeospatialOrientation with both kept it.
Near mapped to depth 1 and far to 0, in projectWorldToScreen's z, for perspective and for orthographic projection.
The arc-rotate and free cameras started with the stated near, far, fov and panningSensibility.
An assigned target leaves worldMatrix stale only until the next alpha/beta/radius write, which then uses the new object and any later writes to it (position x 16 after target.x = 6).
A written target was kept with no input and replaced by position plus the old-yaw unit vector on the next turn.
With two arrows held each axis gets 1/(100*sqrt2), not 1/100 (the sum is normalised), and tabIndex is left alone when the canvas already has a tabindex attribute.

A direct write, a drag and a newer interpolation each made it reject with 'interrupted', and leftover inertia was zeroed on the first frame; a write before the first frame is not between frames and did not interrupt.
Each getter returned the same array, rewritten after a change or another aspect.
beta 0 and -1 stayed until a rotation offset ran, then the frame clamped beta to 0.01 and PI-0.01; no default beta limit exists.
The wheel offset was -deltaY*radius/(wheelPrecision*1000), applied per frame, and radius was floored at 0.01.
The probe and a second test at alpha 0 both moved the target by inertialPanningX*radius/1000 along the camera's right vector, then decayed it by panningInertia.
The y flip holds, but the edges are clamped, not the fractions: {x:-0.5,width:1} gives width 400, not the 800 that clamping x to 0 would give.
Setting camera.viewport left getProjectionMatrix unchanged for the same aspect, and the library's own passes use getEffectiveAspectRatio.
x/y were backing pixels from the top-left including the viewport offset, y grew downwards, and css values were scaled backing values.
Behind gave all three flags, past far gave only clipped, and the off-side x stayed beyond the viewport, unclamped.
A zero viewport width, a zero backingWidth and a lone cssWidth each threw RangeError.
The starting center, radius, pitch, yaw, near/far planes and north +Z all matched.
An in-place center.x write left position unchanged; assigning copied the object and recomputed position.
An interrupted flight resolved, never rejected (the code has no reject path), and the camera kept the radius where it stopped.
With no window it threw ReferenceError; with one, keydown was heard on window only and ArrowUp moved center.z up.
A right drag gave yaw = 50*PI/500 with no coasting and no center move; a left drag panned the center with yaw 0.
radiusMin was 10 for any planetRadius and radius writes were clamped into [10, 4R] at once.
yaw 4 read 4-2*PI and yaw PI read -PI.
Lowered limits apply on the next write only if it changes the value: cam.radius = cam.radius or cam.yaw = cam.yaw is skipped and radius stays 4000.
halfHeight defaulted to 1, null planes followed halfHeight and aspect, fov was ignored, and bound writes showed on the next getProjectionMatrix.
With no enableOrthographicCamera call yet a hand-made ortho was ignored; the call is global, so after one call on any camera a hand-made ortho on another camera counts.
A second enable gave a fresh bounds object, the old one no longer drove the matrix, and disable set ortho to null.
All listed codes moved the camera from canvas keydown, but tabIndex is not set to 0 when the canvas already carries a tabindex attribute (it stayed -1).
Forward climbed along the pitched look direction and Space changed only position.y.
Buttons 0/1/2 turn and pitch clamps, but the turn coasts: a 200 px drag gives 0.1 on the first frame and over 0.9 in total, not dx/angularSensitivity.
Without a scene neither attachFreeControl nor attachConfigurableFreeControl moved the camera.
The per-frame step and coasting hold, but deltaMs is floored at 1, so a frame with deltaMs 0 still moves by speed/sqrt(100000).
_yaw was atan2(dx,dz), writing it left the view matrix unchanged, and the next move rebuilt target from it.
An alpha goal of 2*PI ends exactly unwrapped, but an alpha goal beyond upperAlphaLimit ends on the limit, not exactly on the goal as the note's first clause says.
The step is 1 - 2^(-dt/factor), but a frame with deltaMs 0 or below is taken as 1/60 s, so it still moves instead of standing still as the formula predicts.
Button 1 left all offsets at 0, Ctrl+left rotated without panning, and a touch pointer rotated under primaryButton 'pan'.
Alt+ArrowUp adds 1/25 to inertialRadiusOffset each frame, so held for two frames radius drops 0.04 then 0.076, not 1/25 per frame; only the first frame matches.
A pinch set radius to startRadius*startDistance/distance at once with no scene and inertialRadiusOffset 0.
Only the disposer from the latest setCameraLimits call stops clamping; after a second call, calling the first disposer leaves clamping on (radius = 30 stays 20).
disposeScene left all canvas listeners in place and the returned function removed them.
Rotation inertia ignores deltaMs as said, but the pan offset is not added whole (it is scaled by radius/1000) and decays by panningInertia, not inertia (0.1 became 0.05 with panningInertia 0.5).
fastKeys did nothing without fastMultiplier, and upKeys replaced Space.
Yaw goes the short way and the default is 1000 ms, but a frame with deltaMs 0 counts as 1000/60 ms, so the flight still ends after 61 such frames.
deltaY -1 and -500 gave the same radius, and negative deltaY zoomed in.
A rotate drag during a flight ended it and its promise resolved; an unmapped key, which is no control input, did not.
The pole limit is sin(lat) = 0.998749, about 2.87 degrees (0.05 rad) from the pole, not 0.04 degrees: a center at latitude 88 is moved to 87.13.
At speed 2 the turn coasted to 0.19 on the next frame; at speed 100 it stopped after the first.
